findings.title: SQL expression feature flag is read but ignored
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches. As a result, the SQL expression kill switch always rejects `QueryTypeSQL`, even when the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle is enabled. That leaves the documented feature flag dead and causes users who enable it to still get the internal-looking error `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. If the intent is a permanent hard disable, the flag check should be removed and the documentation/message updated; otherwise this function should return the actual flag value.

findings.title: No regression test for disabled SQL expressions
findings.body: This security fix changes the SQL expression path to reject all SQL, but no test was added or updated to cover the new behavior. A regression test should assert that `QueryTypeSQL` is rejected both when `FlagSqlExpressions` is disabled and when it is enabled, otherwise a future change to `enableSqlExpressions` or the SQL stubs could silently re-enable the vulnerable path.
